requiredFindings.finding: The contracts-v1 recipe retains optionsSha256 7b2bf5ee38ec390564856efbea16c9e43d6ad4de7bd1cc7f49b154709d60d753, the base options hash. The selected candidate options bytes hash to c3481af1bbc9f5c2ec90fff05d1a298452f8901dce5536dd399a1f5fce404af5, which is also the generator-closure pin. tools/contracts/admission.py:269 checks the options file against the recipe hash; tools/generate_contracts.py invokes that registry admission before generation. Thus the exact candidate cannot pass the standard generator entry point even with B-S10 selected. The supplied generation runner calls pipeline.run directly and checks closure/source-set pins but never the recipe options hash, so its successful output evidence does not cover this inconsistency.
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Re-pin contracts-v1.optionsSha256 to the exact candidate options bytes, keep closure/registry/recipe provenance consistent, and refresh the affected product copies, evidence, successor and subject pins. Include the standard recipe-admission check in the evidence path so a stale options pin cannot be bypassed. Preserve the existing schema and resolver boundaries.

nonBlockingObservations.observation: The report-lane paragraph says "It runs in the scratch verification with B-S10 appended." The scratch helper only calls verify_design.verify, and its result explicitly records executedGeneratorCode false and executedRuntimeCode false. It does not run the report TypeScript lane; the retained actual lane log stops at the unbound admission preflight.
nonBlockingObservations.recommendation: Say explicitly that the scratch admission preflight passes with the synthetic appended entry, while the actual report lane remains to be run after real acceptance/assent and selection.
nonBlockingObservations.nonBlockingReason: The check log and scratch JSON accurately expose their execution boundaries; this observation clarifies the README rather than invalidating the recorded structural verification.
